not_scored_why: ROUND 69 RESOLVED THIS AND THE OLD REASON WAS FOUNDED ON A BAD SAMPLE. Round 60 excluded 3 and 5 as '23.3 Lab apart, inseparable'. Measured properly they are 41.1 Lab apart. The 23.3 was the distance between the crimson 3 and a CONTAMINATED crop recorded as the 5: at t=40.01 the two warm balls measure Lab [118,200,178] (the 3, 5 Lab from its entry) and [142,184,192] (the orange 5) - and the old 5 entry [107,176,173] matches NEITHER. It was not a ball colour at all. The 5 is now followed BACKWARD IN POSITION from its own pot, which is the app-independent handle round 60 said was missing: anchored at 157.0s by assigning every trusted reference and taking the single leftover (the pot order fixes the inventory: 1@48.9 2@62.6 3@121.7 4@138.1 5@158.9), then walked back to 40.0s over 1756 samples, aborting on ambiguity - it never aborted. Its colour over that whole span is Lab [145.8,182.5,192.9] sd [2.4,1.8,0.9]. The OTHER warm ball in the pair era is then the 3 by elimination: 44 paired samples, 44/44 of each nearer its own centroid than the other's. VISION-CORROBORATED: the followed ball is plainly orange and the leftover plainly crimson, which is what the shot truth already calls them.
revised_round63: 13 -> 9. The stripe was called a 13 (orange stripe) on the strength of it looking amber next to the BENCH's yellow 9. That is a cross-table comparison and it is invalid: under THIS table's light its own 1 reads amber too (G/R 0.676). Measured WITHIN the table, the stripe's band sits 10.0 Lab from this table's 1 and 98.8 from its 5, so by 'stripe = solid + 8' it is the 9. The same test on the bench returns 1 -> 9, which is the known answer there, so the method is validated on a case with truth. The engine had been right all along and my file was scoring it wrong 61 times.

validated_round84: THE FIVE POTTED BALLS ARE NOW INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED. A ball that vanishes from the cloth at a pot IS the ball that was potted - no colour reference is consulted; each ball is matched only to ITSELF across the four seconds spanning the pot. 2, 3, 4 and 5 land on their own palette entry at 1.4-6.8 Lab with runners-up 36-70 away. THE 1 NEEDED THE STRIPE TEST, for a structural reason worth recording: its colour TWIN the 9 stays on the table, so the disappearance is masked. Within the yellow family the white fractions run 0.048 / 0.051 / 0.395 before the pot and 0.054 / 0.388 after - a LOW-white (solid) member vanished, which is the 1 and not the stripe. Same fact the bench re-derived in round 83: the 9 IS the 1 with a white band. WHAT THIS CANNOT REACH, stated plainly: 6, 7 and 8 are never potted, so the pot order says nothing about them and they remain by-eye from round 60. That is uncomfortable, because round 82 showed the 7 and 8 are named ENTIRELY by colour (166 and 183 names, the identity model reading them 2 of 85 and 0 of 92) - the two most load-bearing references on this table are the two the pot order cannot check.
unreached_round85: 6, 7 and 8 ARE NEVER POTTED, so round 84's pot-order check cannot reach them. Two attempts at something stronger: (1) READING THE PRINTED NUMBER. They are motionless all clip, so 400 frames were averaged per ball to cancel noise. The averages are clean and the colours became unmistakable - but the DIGITS did not. What is visible is the white number CIRCLE, foreshortened onto the ball's upper surface by the overhead view. The control settles it: ball 2, independently confirmed by its pot in round 84, does not read as a '2' either. Method REJECTED - if it cannot read a ball whose answer is known, its reading of an unknown one is worthless. (2) CANONICAL SET. The averaged colours are unambiguous - green, dark red, neutral black - and on a standard set that forces 6/7/8. The only plausible swap was 7 against 8, and they differ on exactly the right axis: the 7 carries 19 units of red chroma (a*=145) while the 8 is neutral (a*=126) and darker (L=10 vs 21). THIS IS WEAKER THAN THE POT ORDER AND THE ASSUMPTION IS NOW EXPLICIT: it holds only if this is a standard-coloured set. It is independent of the APP, which is what round 62's circularity warning was about, but it is not independent of the convention. If Joe ever plays with a non-standard set, these three are the entries that break first.
